why: Telemetry for the start-failure case, and the corpus's first that has to distinguish two zeros that look identical on a dashboard. The crash loop's probe ratio is zero because every probe failed; here `probe_runs_total` is a counter that stops growing, because no probe is ever sent -- the container never reaches a state the platform would probe. Those are different incidents with different repairs, and a corpus that modelled both as 'the probe reading is zero' could not tell them apart, which is exactly the blind spot this case exists to record. `request_rate` is the second zero and a different kind again: it is counted by the router rather than reported by the service, so it stays at zero even though nothing in the service is running to report anything -- a series that a component incapable of serving can still produce. `process_uptime_seconds` is the only reading here with a non-zero post, and its post is a reference to `fault.parameters.containerEntrypointWaitSeconds` rather than a repeated literal: the twenty seconds the ticket states and the twenty seconds the series reports are one number in one place (finding 258). `container_restarts_total` is six rather than the crash loop's 178, and that difference is the kubelet backing off: a container that dies in twenty seconds is rescheduled, not restarted in place, so a high count here would have contradicted the mechanism.

series.why: the checkpoint `cp-probe-never-ran` holds the derived difference of zero: a probe counter that had accumulated 180 samples before the window and did not gain one during it, which is a probe that was never sent rather than one that failed

series.quote: The notification worker has not served a single request since the last rollout
series.why: the checkpoint `cp-no-requests` holds the zero: a rate counted at the router, so zero means no arrival rather than no success, and a service answering errors would still have a rate above zero

the checkpoint `cp-exits-at-twenty` holds the value, and the value is the parameter rather than a second copy of it: the ticket's twenty seconds is the wait bound, and a series that restated it could drift from the declaration

the checkpoint `cp-backoff` holds the total: six attempts in half an hour is what exponential backoff produces, where the crash loop's 178 was restarts in place and a number this size would have been evidence against the mechanism

logs.body: entrypoint: waiting for /var/run/notification-worker/ready.lock, created by the init script of the previous image; not present after 20s, exiting 1
logs.quote: the entrypoint waits for a file the new image no longer creates
logs.why: the entrypoint's own account of what it is waiting for, which is the object a reader can check against the image and the phrase the checkpoint compares rather than a paraphrase of a restart count
